A1.justification: The same authors develop the same ground-state conformation prediction framework and benchmark study through a substantial redesign. Both PDFs are readable, including equations and visual displays. v1 ends with references; v3 includes Appendices A–C. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConfOpt prediction results on Molecule3D and QM9, loss ablations, runtime comparisons and iteration experiments in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v3 reports original WGFormer benchmark results, architecture and loss ablations, runtime comparisons, and noise and hyperparameter robustness experiments, including Appendix C.

M1.justification: v1 uses graph-token embeddings and recurrent Transformer blocks with softmax attention. v3 replaces these with atom-type embeddings and WGFormer layers using tied queries/keys, values derived from -WW^T, Sinkhorn normalization, symmetric relations and no FFN. The residual coordinate decoder is retained, but coordinate MAE plus weighted distance MAE becomes distance MAE plus weighted coordinate RMSD.

E1.justification: Molecule3D and QM9 remain the evaluated datasets for ground-state conformation prediction. v3 adds testing with Gaussian perturbations to QM9 input coordinates (Section 6.3, Figure 6), extending coverage to noisy-input conditions. The other added experiments remain within the existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes RDKit ETKDG as a scored baseline and adds SE(3)-Transformer, EGNN, ConfOpt-TwoAtom and ConfOpt-ThreeAtom. GINE, GATv2, GPS and GTMGC remain. The added ConfOpt baselines cite Guan et al.'s Energy-inspired molecular conformation optimization and are distinct from v1's proposed ConfOpt. Comparator membership also changes in the visual and runtime comparisons.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits and three evaluation metrics remain unchanged. However, v3 replaces the QM9 K-iteration study with intermediate-layer evaluation of separately trained 10- and 30-layer models. It adds controlled Sinkhorn/QKV combinations, Gaussian perturbations during inference, and batch-size/learning-rate sweeps. These substantially expand the experimental protocols; newly disclosed default settings alone do not establish changes to earlier settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds attention-component ablations, noise robustness, hyperparameter sensitivity and atom-count analysis (Table 3 and Figures 6–9). It removes v1's graph-guidance ablation using ConfOpt-3D, narrows the loss ablation from all three benchmark settings to random-split Molecule3D, and replaces iteration analysis with a layer-depth comparison. The questions tested and supporting analyses are substantially revised.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands for performance. v3's Gaussian-noise standard deviations specify input perturbations, rather than uncertainty in estimated results.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the proposed-model test C-RMSD entries of 0.697/0.685/0.212 with WGFormer entries of 0.664/0.627/0.206 for Molecule3D random/scaffold and QM9. These concern different models and objectives, rather than reruns under identical conditions. Common 2D baseline scores remain unchanged, while new 3D comparator results and revised runtime, ablation, depth and robustness findings substantially change the reported evidence.

T1.justification: v1 contains model, loss and metric equations without comparable gradient-flow theory. v3 adds measure and energy definitions, continuous-time derivations, Propositions 4.1–4.2 for Dirac/non-Dirac cases, and proofs in Appendix B, plus an SE(3)-equivariance proof in Appendix A. The new Eq. 16 has an unresolved entropy-sign inconsistency between its purportedly equivalent energy expressions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift the central contribution from graph-guided conformation optimization with joint supervision to an interpretable Wasserstein-gradient-flow-driven Transformer. v3 newly claims to bridge energy-based simulation and learning and to introduce this gradient-flow perspective to ground-state prediction. The broad claim of superior accuracy and efficiency is retained.

C2.justification: v3 introduces interpretations of latent energy and entropy, depth as optimization resolution, and FFN removal as an efficiency mechanism. It adds explanations of noise/hyperparameter robustness and molecule-size effects. Section 4.2 explicitly limits gradient-flow correspondence for non-Dirac measures as M tends to infinity. These substantially extend v1's empirical interpretations of graph guidance, joint supervision and iteration.

D1.justification: v1 provides equations and pseudocode but little concrete training configuration. v3 supplies exact split sizes, GPU and checkpoint-selection information, model dimensions, 500-epoch budgets, batch sizes, learning rates, Adam settings and loss weights (Section 6.1 and Appendix C). Its abstract also adds a code-access link. These are substantial documentation additions, although the actual Sinkhorn iteration count remains unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 acknowledges prior conformation-optimization methods, including Guan et al.'s ConfOpt, and adds REBIND, Sinkformers, optimal transport and differential-equation literature. It substantially reduces the earlier survey of molecular representation learning and positions the contribution around interpretable gradient-flow architecture. This revises the novelty argument beyond merely expanding citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten around WGFormer. v1's unified Method section becomes separate model, theoretical-analysis and learning sections; its pseudocode is removed, and metric definitions move to Appendix C. The explanatory narrative and organization change substantially beyond accommodating additional results.

P2.justification: The conceptual and architecture diagrams are replaced, molecular examples and runtime charts are redrawn with different comparators, and the optimization plot changes axes and series. Table 1 gains 2D/3D grouping and highlighted rows, while the loss table is restructured. v3 also adds an architecture-ablation table, dataset/hyperparameter tables, and noise, distribution and sensitivity plots.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v1's sparse implementation reporting and limited comparison against other conformation-optimization methods, while adding useful controlled ablations and robustness tests. However, its central new gradient-flow justification contains an unresolved inconsistency: Eq. 16 reverses the entropy sign between expressions claimed to be equivalent, also repeated in Appendix B.1. Because this affects the revision's main interpretability claim, the substantial documentation and empirical benefits do not establish a reliably assessable net quality improvement.
